beats.say: You want to learn Kubernetes. But a cloud cluster costs money every hour.
And you already know Docker. So start there.
beats.label: Good news
beats.head: You already know Docker

beats.say: This port gives you three things: the tools, a cluster, and an image to sail with.
beats.label: Port 0 · Shipyard setup

check.prompt: On kind, what is a Kubernetes node?
check.why: kind means Kubernetes in Docker. Each node is one container on your laptop.

beats.say: First: where does the cluster run?
A tool named kind runs every Kubernetes node as one Docker container.
beats.label: kind
beats.head: A node is a container

beats.say: You start three nodes: one control plane and two workers.
beats.label: Three nodes
beats.head: One control plane, two workers

beats.say: It is free, it starts in a minute, and you can delete it at any time.
beats.label: Why kind
beats.head: Free, fast, safe to break

beats.say: kind builds the cluster. You use it a few times.
beats.label: Tool one
beats.head: kind builds the cluster

beats.say: The second tool talks to the cluster. You use it all day, on any cluster.
beats.label: Tool two
beats.head: kubectl talks to the cluster

check.prompt: Your pod cannot pull an image you built on your laptop. What did you miss?
options: docker push to a public registry
check.why: A kind node has its own image store. kind load copies your image into it.

beats.say: Third: the image you take through every port.
Tugboat is a small web app. You deploy it, scale it, break it and secure it.
beats.label: tugboat
beats.head: One app for the whole course

beats.say: A kind node cannot see the images on your laptop. So you load the image into the nodes.
beats.label: The trap
beats.head: Load the image into the nodes

beats.say: A node is a container. One tool builds, one tool talks. And load your image.
beats.label: Shipyard setup

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
